item.title: No25, no15, others on the street, 30th September
item.description:
There are a number of houses with overgrown hedges that fall beyond the boundary wall of the house onto the public pavement. Please could you issue a notice to the houses with hedges growing beyond their boundary walls to trim these down such that they do not encroach on the public pavement, and if they do not comply then the council needs to take the action themselves. Thank you.

item.title: Large Tree blocking footpath and damaging front garden, 30th September
item.description:
We would like to request an inspection and remedial works to the large council-owned tree immediately outside the property of 134 Friern Road, SE22 0AY. The tree has now become extremely large for its position and is having a significant impact on both the pavement and our property. As shown in the attached photographs, the mature trunk occupies a substantial part of the pavement and leans across the footway, considerably reducing the usable width available to pedestrians, particularly anyone using a wheelchair, mobility aid or pushchair. We are also seeing cracking and movement to the masonry boundary wall and concrete within our front garden immediately adjacent to the tree. Given the size and proximity of the tree and its root system, we are concerned that its continued growth may be contributing to this damage and would like this assessed by a Tree Officer. The tree also has a very large and dense canopy extending towards and across the front of the property, substantially reducing natural light to our front garden and ground-floor rooms. Given the combination of its size, position, obstruction of the footway, apparent impact on the surrounding hard surfaces/boundary wall and the extent of the canopy, we would like Southwark Council to consider removing the tree and replacing it with a smaller, more appropriately sized species. If removal is not considered appropriate, we would ask that substantial pruning/crown reduction and any other appropriate works are carried out to reduce its impact on the property and pavement. We would be grateful if a Tree Officer could inspect the tree in person rather than the report being assessed solely from photographs, particularly given the visible cracking and movement around the property boundary.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 95, Friern Road, East Dulwich, Greater London

item.title: Unannounced tree surgery, 30th September
item.description:
Unannounced tree surgery in Sparrow Wood behind 27 Hollingworth Road, BR5 1AQ. Some unannounced tree surgery has taken place in Sparrow Wood, Petts Wood, behind our house at 27 Hollingworth Road, BR5 1AQ. The tree being pruned is in the woods immediately behind our house and its branches overhang into our garden and our neighbours at 29 Hollingworth Road. On speaking to the workmen, they told us they were from Bromley Council and that we should have been informed well in advance. We think our neighbours may have asked for the tree to be cut back as it affects their property more than ours, and that they may have been informed about the work rather than us. Please confirm that it was Bromley Council workers carrying out this work. We also note that they stood on the roof of our garden shed whilst carrying out the work and entered our property without our permission. Our garden shed is of a sturdy plastic construction, and we hope that no damage has occurred to it. Regards, David Carnochan
